subject.title: [Bug] Silent degradation on failed Tailscale bind during startup

question: Should failure to establish explicitly requested Tailscale exposure terminate the Gateway, or should the Gateway remain locally available while reporting a degraded startup state?
rationale: Current documentation intentionally preserves loopback availability, while the proposed fatal behavior changes startup and supervisor semantics; source inspection cannot determine which availability tradeoff maintainers want.

options.title: Keep Safe Fallback
options.body: Keep the Gateway loopback-only, but make failed Tailscale exposure visible in startup outcomes, readiness, status, and diagnostics.

options.title: Fail Startup
options.body: Treat any explicitly requested Tailscale Serve, Funnel, or direct Tailnet setup failure as fatal and document the availability change.

options.title: Split Semantics
options.body: Keep direct Tailnet fallback locally available while making managed Serve/Funnel failures fatal.

recommendation.title: Keep Safe Fallback
recommendation.body: Keep the Gateway loopback-only, but make failed Tailscale exposure visible in startup outcomes, readiness, status, and diagnostics.

likelyOwner.reason: The feature history ties this person to the original Tailnet bind behavior and several subsequent Tailscale security and status decisions.
